title: Physics-Informed Generative World Models for Real-Time Bidding: Deriving Statistical Laws from First Principles

problem.claim: Reliable policy optimization in real-time bidding requires a high-fidelity world model that simulates stochastic market dynamics under constraints.

gap.claim: Current generative simulators rely on deterministic point-prediction objectives and fail to capture extreme mean-dependent heteroscedasticity and structural coupling among feedback variables.

contributions.claim: Introduces a physics-informed statistical modeling framework for real-time bidding derived from first principles.
Operationalizes Poisson-lognormal and Tweedie-lognormal marginal laws into an efficient zero-inflated generalized beta of the second kind surrogate.
Uses a normalizing-flow copula to model non-Gaussian tail dependence between cost and value arising from shared winning events.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on large-scale production datasets reportedly achieve state-of-the-art distributional fidelity.
The framework reportedly exhibits clear neural scaling laws.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reliable RTB policy optimization requires a high-fidelity stochastic world model under constraints.
Existing generative simulators use deterministic objectives that are statistically ill-posed for auction data and miss key distributional structure.
The paper proposes a first-principles physics-informed statistical framework with specified marginal distributions and a ZI-GB2 surrogate.
The formulation models variance scaling and uses a normalizing-flow copula for non-Gaussian dependence between cost and value.
The authors report strong distributional fidelity and neural scaling laws on large-scale production datasets.

source_observation.claim: Modeling variance scaling explicitly is presented as a way to resolve gradient dominance in heteroscedastic regression.

interpretation.claim: When outcome variance changes sharply with the mean, distribution-aware objectives may be more suitable than deterministic point prediction.

application.claim: Consider explicit variance modeling when building stochastic simulators for similarly heteroscedastic feedback data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach transfers beyond the reported RTB setting or production datasets.

source_observation.claim: The reported dependence between cost and value is attributed to shared winning events and modeled with a normalizing-flow copula.

interpretation.claim: Shared latent or event-level causes can require dependence models that capture non-Gaussian tail behavior.

application.claim: For coupled outcomes with shared events, evaluate explicit copula or other joint-distribution modeling rather than independent marginal models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide quantitative details about the tail-dependence fit or comparisons with alternative copulas.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the production datasets, sample sizes, or data-generation conditions.
The abstract does not identify baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative gains.
The abstract does not provide derivations, assumptions, or proof details for the stated statistical laws.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
